title: Custom CPU Emulator & Assembler
description: For a second-year Computer Architecture project at Humber, I designed a custom Assembly language, wrote an assembler to convert it into machine-code binaries, and built a software CPU emulator to execute those programs. The project was based on CPU architecture concepts taught in class, but the implementation was my own. I modeled the interface after DOS debug.exe, originally built the project on AIX with GCC, and later ported and continued it independently in Turbo C++ for DOS.

sections.title: Individual Computer Architecture Project
paragraphs: This was an individual project from my second-year Computer Architecture coursework at Humber.
The class and textbooks explained how CPUs work, but we were responsible for designing and implementing our own software model.

sections.title: Custom Assembly Language
paragraphs: I created my own Assembly-style instruction syntax for the emulator.
The instruction set was designed around the CPU concepts covered in class while leaving the specific implementation decisions up to me.

sections.title: Custom Assembler
paragraphs: I wrote an assembler that converted the custom Assembly source into the binary machine-code format understood by the emulator.
The original legacy card described this as a compiler, but assembler is the more precise term for the implementation.

sections.title: Software CPU Emulator
paragraphs: The emulator executed the generated machine-code files and modeled the major internal components expected in a simple CPU.

sections.title: debug.exe-Inspired Interface
paragraphs: I chose to model the user interface after DOS debug.exe.
That gave the project a low-level interactive feel appropriate for inspecting and executing machine state.

sections.title: AIX / GCC Development
paragraphs: The original school version was developed on AIX using GCC.

sections.title: Turbo C++ DOS Port
paragraphs: After completing the coursework, I ported the project to Turbo C++ for DOS and continued working on it independently because I enjoyed the project.
